step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified all architecture components from visual whiteboard representation and audio transcript: Mobile Client (UserConsumerMobile), Application Load Balancer (ALB), ECS Fargate (ECS), Relational Database Service (RDS), ElastiCache, AWS Lambda, and Amazon CloudWatch.
2. Normalized all service names strictly to the allowed vocabulary list.
3. Extracted performance and architecture notes from the audio (e.g., handling ~60,000 requests/min average, serverless container execution on Fargate, logging and metric collection with zero operational overhead).
4. Formatted request processing and data persistence interactions into Flow 0, and observability telemetry into Flow 1.

graph.name: Social Quantum Serverless Game Backend Architecture
graph.categories: Game Development, Serverless, Containers, Caching, Relational Database
graph.notes: Architecture for Social Quantum's mobile games processing an average of 60,000 requests per minute using AWS serverless services.

nodes.name: Mobile Client
nodes.notes: Generates an average of 60,000 requests per minute (varying between 10,000 and 120,000 req/min).

nodes.name: ALB
nodes.notes: Entry point handling HTTP requests and forwarding them to the ECS Fargate application cluster.

nodes.name: ECS Fargate
nodes.notes: Core containerized application logic running serverless on AWS Fargate, responsible for game logic and user interaction.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: RDS Postgres database cluster storing persistent user and game data.

nodes.name: ElastiCache
nodes.notes: In-memory Redis cache used to reduce database load.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Serverless functions executing infrequent or scheduled maintenance tasks.

nodes.name: CloudWatch
nodes.notes: Centralized logging and metrics monitoring service across all backend components.

edges.notes: Mobile client sends incoming game request traffic to the ALB.
ALB routes user requests to ECS Fargate containers.
ECS Fargate reads and writes persistent user and game data to RDS.
ECS Fargate retrieves and caches dynamic data in ElastiCache for Redis.
Bi-directional relationship for database caching and cache updates.
ECS Fargate triggers or integrates with Lambda functions for maintenance tasks.
ECS Fargate pushes container metrics and application logs to CloudWatch.
Lambda function execution logs and metrics are forwarded to CloudWatch.
